title: Case Q-10231: Recurring Grid Fault Shutdown
answer: Similar resolved case (Ticket #Q-10231): inverter displayed 'Grid Fault' (E03) and shut down repeatedly. Root cause was utility voltage fluctuating outside the inverter's anti-islanding threshold. Resolution: after the utility confirmed line voltage was within ANSI C84.1 range, L2 support adjusted the inverter's grid-protection settings within the IEEE 1547 allowable window — this setting isn't installer-accessible, so this case required escalation rather than a power cycle.

title: Case Q-10287: Hail-Damaged Panel String
answer: Similar resolved case (Ticket #Q-10287): two panels in a 10-panel string showed near-zero output in monitoring after a hail event. An IV curve tracer confirmed micro-cracking in both panels. Resolution: both panels were replaced under the 25-year product warranty and an RMA was processed — document the hail date and any homeowner insurance claim number, since warranty and insurance claims are handled on separate tracks.

title: Case Q-10312: System Shows Offline After Router Update
answer: Similar resolved case (Ticket #Q-10312): homeowner reported the monitoring app showed 'system offline' for 3 days. Root cause was a home router firmware update that changed the SSID broadcast settings, dropping the inverter's Wi-Fi connection. Resolution: re-paired the inverter's Wi-Fi dongle to the network using the SSID/password shown in the router's admin page — the inverter itself was operating normally the entire time, only reporting was affected.

title: Case Q-10355: Battery Stuck at 20% State of Charge
answer: Similar resolved case (Ticket #Q-10355): a Q.HOME ESS battery would not charge past 20% state of charge. Root cause was a known BMS (Battery Management System) firmware bug affecting the charge algorithm on early HYB-G3 units. Resolution: a remote firmware push via the Q.OMMAND portal resolved it fully — no truck roll was needed. If a battery you're servicing shows this symptom, check the firmware version first before scheduling a site visit.

title: Case Q-10402: Rapid Shutdown Failed Inspection
answer: Similar resolved case (Ticket #Q-10402): the rapid shutdown device failed its initiation test during inspection. Root cause was a loose RSD transmitter wiring connection at the combiner box. Resolution: re-terminated the connections and confirmed voltage dropped within the 30-second/30V spec at the array boundary; the system passed re-inspection the same day. Always torque-check RSD wiring specifically — it's a common miss during otherwise-complete installs.

title: Case Q-10460: DC Arc Fault From Rodent Damage
answer: Similar resolved case (Ticket #Q-10460): inverter threw E04 'DC Arc Fault Detected'. Root cause was rodent damage — something had chewed through DC wiring insulation near the junction box, causing intermittent arcing. Resolution: replaced the damaged conduit run and added rodent guards at all conduit entry points. De-energize the string immediately if E04 appears; do not attempt to re-energize until the wiring has been physically inspected.

title: Case Q-10489: Production Below PVWatts Estimate
answer: Similar resolved case (Ticket #Q-10489): a new install produced 15% below the original PVWatts estimate. Root cause was tree growth causing afternoon shading that wasn't present (or wasn't accounted for) at the original design/survey stage. Resolution: no equipment fault was found — recommended tree trimming to the homeowner. This is a useful case to reference when a homeowner disputes production estimates on an otherwise healthy system.

title: Case Q-10512: Firmware Update Stuck at 40%
answer: Similar resolved case (Ticket #Q-10512): a firmware update on a Q.VOLT inverter was stuck at 40% for over 2 hours. Root cause was the update being interrupted by a momentary power blip. Resolution: a manual power cycle followed by re-initiating the push from the Q.OMMAND portal completed the update successfully. If a push has been stuck for under 30 minutes, wait it out first — most transient stalls clear on their own.

title: Case Q-10530: Serial Number Not Found During Commissioning
answer: Similar resolved case (Ticket #Q-10530): the monitoring portal showed 'Serial Number Not Found' during commissioning. Root cause was a shipping/registration lag — the unit hadn't yet been entered into Qcells' production database. Resolution: escalated to logistics and the serial was activated within 24 hours. If this happens, don't reflash or replace the unit — confirm the serial against the physical label first, then escalate rather than troubleshoot further.

title: Case Q-10567: Burning Smell Near Inverter (Safety)
answer: Similar resolved case (Ticket #Q-10567) — SAFETY: homeowner reported a burning smell near the inverter. Immediate advisory was given to de-energize the system at the AC and DC disconnects and avoid the area. An emergency technician was dispatched; root cause was a loose AC terminal lug causing arcing. Resolution: the electrician replaced the terminal and re-torqued all AC connections; the inverter tested normal afterward. Any report of burning smell, smoke, or visible arcing should be treated as urgent and escalated immediately — do not attempt phone troubleshooting first.
